principles: One-shot convergence without rerunning project commands
Fail closed outside the exact canonical lifecycle transaction
drivers: Remove the observed mandatory manual metadata commit and retry
Preserve canonical PASS receipt integrity and CAS semantics
Avoid trusting unsigned phase_transition event shape

options.name: A: transition-owned atomic closeout
pros: The transition knows exactly which lifecycle files it generated
Verifier can retain strict rejection of every pre-existing dirty path
No new trust format or migration
cons: Adds a canonical metadata commit to TEST transition
Must prove the commit does not stale review or include unrelated dirt

options.name: B: receipt-bound reuse transaction admission
pros: Could combine transition and reuse writes
cons: No signed phase_transition receipt exists today
Adding a proof format would broaden this correction

options.name: C: permit metadata-only dirty paths generically
cons: Would absorb human, forged or unrelated lifecycle metadata

rationale: Scope review confirmed phase_transition is an unsigned JSONL append, so verifier cannot distinguish it safely from forged event-shaped dirt. The transition orchestrator is the causal owner and must atomically close only its freshly generated TEST lifecycle files before returning. The verifier remains unchanged and fail-closed for any dirty state present at validate entry.

preMortem.scenario: The transition commit stages unrelated user changes.
preMortem.trigger: It uses the real index or a broad story-directory glob.
preMortem.mitigation: Use the isolated immutable metadata writer with an exact generated path allowlist and preserve real-index bytes.

preMortem.scenario: A forged process event becomes trusted by shape.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation checks event type or prose in verifier.
preMortem.consequence: External dirt is adopted into PASS evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Do not admit pre-existing verifier dirt; trust stays with transition-owned writes only.

preMortem.scenario: TEST transition metadata commit invalidates current review evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Hashes treat canonical lifecycle metadata as story material or lineage rejects the commit.
preMortem.consequence: One retry is replaced by re-review churn.
preMortem.mitigation: Assert trusted-story-metadata-descendant lineage, unchanged storyFilesHash and fresh reviewer receipts after transition.

preMortem.scenario: Writer/CAS/hook failure leaves partial metadata or reports TEST success.
preMortem.trigger: Transition state is persisted before commit failure is handled atomically.
preMortem.consequence: Story phase and Git evidence diverge.
preMortem.mitigation: Fail transition loudly, restore exact worktree/index state, and cover concurrent HEAD and hook mutation paths.
